initialUserIntent: Make RefactorKit Java refactoring operational as an IDE product feature (user-authorized APR-DECISION-REFACTORKIT-PRODUCT-FEATURE-001). Complete the JetBrains-style Java IDE management: expose deterministic Java refactoring operations (rename class/member/local-var, move class, change method signature, safe delete; plus the existing scan/symbol/definition/references/diagnostics surface) through the RefactorKit daemon, with preview -> apply -> rollback, honest unavailable, and web-first boundary. RefactorKit engine (installed /home/paperboy/workspace/refactorkit) supports full Java refactoring; this slice makes it operational in the IDE surface.

User authorized RefactorKit as a PRODUCT FEATURE (Java/RefactorKit product-surface in scope within bdd-ts). Java TEST infra (JavaSpec, Maven, JUnit-specific policy, Java datasets) and Java-only RefactorKit rules as the workflow's own refactoring authority remain EXCLUDED.

requirement.title: Operational RefactorKit Java refactoring in the IDE (preview -> apply -> rollback)
requirement.classification: Story BDD + Spec BDD for pure view-model decisions
requirement.capability: Expose deterministic Java refactoring operations (rename class/member/local-variable, move class, change method signature, safe delete) through the RefactorKit daemon behind provider-neutral frontend ports. The IDE requests a preview patch plan for a selected symbol/range, presents it read-only, applies it on explicit authority, and supports rollback where advertised. Honest unavailable when the RefactorKit capability is absent or the operation is unsupported. No hidden domain policy in adapters.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Given a Java symbol/selection, the IDE requests a preview patch plan for a named refactoring operation (rename, move class, change signature, safe delete) and presents it read-only before any apply; no write occurs before explicit user/authority approval.
Apply binds to the exact reviewed plan and authority; the result is reported honestly (applied vs rejected) and rollback is supported only when the daemon advertises it.
The flow follows extract -> delegate -> response with no hidden domain policy; absent capability or unsupported operation reports honest unavailable/error, never fabricated success.
Boundary invariant: packages/ui, packages/web-core, apps/web never import @tauri-apps/api; browser/Tauri RefactorKit implementations live behind frontend ports.
Status is evidence-based with an explicit state, never inferred from shells; live Tauri-window Java refactoring E2E may remain unvalidated if headless (recorded honestly).

requirement.owner: bdd-ts-domain-expert (domain research) + bdd-ts-gherkin-writer (feature) + ts-story-driven (Story) + ts-spec-driven (view-model Spec) + tauri-rust-coder (daemon commands) + tauri-adapter-coder + browser-adapter-coder + frontend-core-coder/frontend-ui-coder (view-model + UI)
requirement.scope: RefactorKit Java refactoring operations (rename/move-class/change-signature/safe-delete) as a coherent first slice, reusing the existing daemon preview/apply/rollback infrastructure. The existing scan/symbol/definition/references/diagnostics surface stays as-is (no rework). Java navigation go-to-definition/references and Java build/run/debug and project model remain separate later slices.
exclusions: JavaSpec, Maven, JUnit-specific policy, Java datasets as workflow test infra
Java-only RefactorKit rules as the workflow's own refactoring authority
RefactorKit TS-only diagnostics/symbols rework (existing surface unchanged)
Java navigation, Java build/run/debug, project model (later slices)
openQuestions: Operation scope: which operations are first-class in this slice (rename class/member/local-var, move class, change signature, safe delete) — confirm the set.

Preview source: whether the preview patch plan comes from the deterministic daemon fixture or the real refactorkit engine in this environment; if only fixture/harness evidence is available, the real-engine path stays honest-unavailable/unit-evidenced.
Editor wiring: whether Java refactoring UX is proven wired into the live editor or a desktop-harness renderer is acceptable evidence.
Authority: confirm apply requires explicit user/authority approval bound to the exact reviewed plan (no auto-apply).
